correctness.rationale: The formula is an exact Gaussian Fourier transform. The derivative stationarity equation has an entire power series whose coefficients undergo at most one negative-to-positive sign change. Strict monotonicity after division by the first positive monomial proves zero or one positive stationary amplitude point globally. Signs at zero and at the unique off-center maximum classify exactly one, two or three real-intensity maxima and the boundary degeneracies. Analytic expansions prove the two onset laws. A saved-package checker independently tests 212 finite symbolic and numeric identities; no finite experiment substitutes for the analytic proof.

value.rationale: This is the natural complete two-parameter resolution phase diagram at the exact destructive-interference time for the minimal three-tone Gaussian-window signal. It separates outer-peak splitting from middle-phase-cancellation recovery, supplies exact thresholds and global peak multiplicity, and quantifies both new branches. Its relevance is structural and quantitative, not merely an arbitrary finite computation; it does not assert noise-robust detection or an all-time ridge theorem.
